org_name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
title: Sweep: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET) — ai-safety funder
summary: CSET, a Georgetown University policy research center, runs a Foundational Research Grants program funding exploration of foundational technical topics tied to the long-term national-security implications of AI. It sits alongside the other AI-safety grantmakers already tracked (Coefficient Giving, FLI, Schmidt Sciences) but is not itself in the registry.

org_name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
title: Sweep: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET) — Foundational Research Grants (ai-safety)
summary: CSET's Foundational Research Grants program funds exploration of foundational technical AI-safety-adjacent topics with national-security relevance.

title: Sweep: AI Risk Mitigation Fund (ARM Fund) — ai-safety funder
summary: The AI Risk Mitigation Fund is a nonprofit that makes grants toward technical AI-alignment research, AI policy work, and training programs for new researchers, aiming to reduce catastrophic risk from advanced AI. It is a smaller, newer entrant alongside the larger AI-safety funders already tracked in the registry.

title: Sweep: Alchemy — arbitrum funder
summary: Alchemy, a Web3 developer-infrastructure company, runs an Arbitrum-specific grant offering up to $500,000 in platform credits per team building on Arbitrum Orbit chains. It is a multi-chain infra provider rather than a pure grants foundation, so confidence is moderate.

title: Sweep: Alchemy — Alchemy + Arbitrum Grant (arbitrum)
summary: Alchemy offers up to $500K in infrastructure credits, first-come-first-served, to teams building Orbit chains on Arbitrum.

title: Sweep: Arbitrum Gaming Ventures — arbitrum funder
summary: Arbitrum Gaming Ventures is an investment vehicle seeded via Arbitrum DAO's Gaming Catalyst Program, backing teams building blockchain games on Arbitrum; it announced a $10M first cohort of investments. It is equity/investment-style funding rather than classic non-dilutive grants, and appears to be an Arbitrum Foundation/DAO-affiliated offshoot rather than a fully independent funder, so treat this one with more scrutiny.

title: Sweep: Intersect (Intersect MBO) — cardano funder
summary: Intersect is the member-based organization now stewarding Cardano protocol development and coordinating the community budget process, including facilitating Project Catalyst / on-chain treasury withdrawal proposals. The registry's own cardano.yaml system note names Intersect as one of the ecosystem's core funding bodies, but it has no org entry yet.

title: Sweep: Intersect (Intersect MBO) — Project Catalyst (cardano)
summary: Project Catalyst is Cardano's on-chain treasury funding system, which has distributed over $150M in ada to community-proposed projects since 2020 through recurring quarterly rounds; stewardship of the fund has shifted to Intersect.

title: Sweep: EMURGO — cardano funder
summary: EMURGO is one of Cardano's three founding entities; it invests in and funds Web3/blockchain startups building on Cardano through vehicles like a $100M ecosystem investment fund and regional programs such as EMURGO Africa's accelerator and hackathon grants.

title: Sweep: Green Climate Fund — climate funder
summary: The Green Climate Fund is the world's largest dedicated climate fund, established under the UN climate framework to invest in low-emission, climate-resilient projects in developing countries. It is a major international funder not yet tracked under the registry's climate domain.

title: Sweep: Giving Green Fund — climate funder
summary: Giving Green Fund pools donor money and regrants it to vetted climate nonprofits working on clean energy and industrial decarbonization; it announced $1.94M in grants in February 2026. It operates in the same effective-giving-adjacent lane as other funds the registry already tracks.

title: Sweep: Youth Climate Justice Fund — climate funder
summary: The Youth Climate Justice Fund makes grants to youth-led climate justice organizing. It is a smaller, less-established funder than the registry's existing climate entries, so this candidate is weaker and worth double-checking before promotion.

title: Sweep: Climate Resilience Fund — climate funder
summary: The Climate Resilience Fund supports community climate-resilience work in the US, building on tools like NOAA's Climate Program Office resilience toolkit. Evidence of a formal, sizeable grants program is thinner than for the other climate candidates in this batch, so flag for extra scrutiny.

title: Sweep: European Research Council (ERC) — eu-public-rd funder
summary: The European Research Council is the EU's flagship basic-research funder, awarding Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Synergy, and Proof-of-Concept grants to researchers across all fields, including AI. It operates within Horizon Europe but has its own identity, governance, and website distinct from the generic Horizon Europe entry already tracked.

title: Sweep: European Innovation Council (EIC) — eu-public-rd funder
summary: The European Innovation Council funds breakthrough, high-risk deep-tech innovation through instruments like EIC Pathfinder (research grants), EIC Transition (market-readiness grants), and EIC Accelerator (grant plus equity investment for startups/SMEs). Like the ERC, it runs under the Horizon Europe umbrella but is a distinct funding body not yet tracked.

title: Sweep: European Innovation Council (EIC) — EIC Accelerator (eu-public-rd)
summary: EIC Accelerator funds startups and SMEs with high-risk, high-impact deep-tech innovations, combining a grant of up to EUR 2.5M with an optional equity investment component.

org_name: Filecoin Foundation for the Decentralized Web (FFDW)
title: Sweep: Filecoin Foundation for the Decentralized Web (FFDW) — filecoin funder
summary: FFDW is a separate 501(c)(3) nonprofit from Filecoin Foundation that has awarded roughly $23M across 20 grants to open-source/decentralized-web and journalism-infrastructure projects (e.g. Freedom of the Press Foundation's SecureDrop). It is closely related in branding to the already-tracked Filecoin Foundation but is a legally distinct funder, and recent public activity looks slower than 2020-2023, so verify it's still actively granting before promoting.

orgs/filecoin-foundation-for-the-decentr.name: Filecoin Foundation for the Decentralized Web (FFDW)
